To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CMV contributes to gliobastoma progression in the context of loss of tumor suppressor genes.
CMV infection increases glioblastoma growth in the context of loss of tumor suppressors in mice, and this effect may be mediated through STAT3.
CMV infection in the context of glioma tumor suppressor mutations accelerates glioma formation and progression by activating the STAT3 pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cytomegarovirus in glioblastomas and the mechanisms by which it may contribute to tumor progression.
the role of the cytomegaloviruses, MCMV and HCMV, as a cofactor in the genesis of the glioblastoma.
the role of CMV infection in glioblastomas in humans and in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CMV infection is associated with glioma formation/ progression, at least under some circumstances.
the role of CMV infection in gliomas is not a direct one, but it is a consequence of the activation of STAT3 signaling, which is known to be a key driver of glioma formation.
CMV infection in the context of glioma suppressors is detrimental to the host and that the virus contributes to glioma formation/ progression in mice and possibly also in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CMV is a tumor promoter in the context of glioblastoma and that STAT3 is an important mediator of CMV effects in glioma cells.
CMV is a glioma promoter, and this is due to STAT3 activation.
MCMV infection of Mut3 mice results in a shortened survival time from their tumors compared with controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CMV infection in the context of glioma suppressor mutations can accelerate the formation of glioblastoma.
CMV can contribute to glioblastomas in the setting of tumor suppressor loss, and that this is mediated in part via STAT3.

, although cytomegaloviruses are neurotropic viruses that infect neural stem cells, they do not appear to contribute to glioblastomas in the context of a normal brain, but they do contribute to glioblasotma formation in the context of mutations in tumor suppressors.
